cases.contract: Different base seeds produce diversity in at least one eligible controlled choice while each seed remains exactly replayable.
Crash-state exploration enumerates every valid state for bounded small operation sets lazily, without duplicates, and can resume from a checkpoint.
cases.replacement: V2 test loops demonstrate expected small crash states but do not define a bounded resumable enumeration identity; v3 requires canonical state identities, explicit bounds, and resumable checkpoints.

cases.contract: File sync persists file data and metadata dependencies, while directory sync separately persists namespace entries and parent-directory dependencies.
cases.replacement: V2 contains questioned directory-sync expectations; v3 records file and directory durability as separate explicit dependency closures and rejects ambiguous host-filesystem inference.

cases.contract: Every directed link applies its configured deterministic delay to delivery and records that delay in replayable network transitions.
Graceful stop follows explicit shutdown semantics; harsh crash revokes the exact incarnation and deterministically breaks its established and pending TCP operations.
cases.replacement: V2 observes broken connections but does not bind all in-flight packets to an incarnation; v3 rejects delivery from a crashed incarnation and distinguishes stop from crash in lifecycle records.

cases.contract: Each node has a stable identity and address across lifecycle transitions, and every start or restart creates a distinct monotonically increasing incarnation handle.
cases.replacement: V2 exposes machine pointers and translator-era lifecycle behavior; v3 uses stable serializable node identities and explicit incarnation handles so stale work can be rejected.

cases.contract: A bounded deterministic nemesis can repeatedly partition and heal links and crash or restart selected node incarnations with every action recorded for exact replay.
cases.replacement: V2 combines random nemesis behavior with implicit machine state; v3 requires bounded action plans, stable target identities, explicit eligible alternatives, and exact replay records.

cases.contract: A crash selects only a dependency-valid subset of pending durable operations, applies it atomically, and records the selected canonical persistence state.
Directional partition causes deterministic timeout or refusal according to connection phase; healing permits a new connection without reviving stale incarnation traffic.
cases.replacement: V2 connectivity leaves symmetry and unreachable-versus-rejected outcomes implicit; v3 models directional links, connection phase, deadlines, and heal/reconnect transitions explicitly.

cases.contract: Rename and truncate contribute explicit namespace, file-content, file-metadata, and directory dependencies to the set of valid post-crash states.
cases.replacement: V2 enumerates examples but leaves some rename and directory-sync outcomes as questioned expectations; v3 derives all valid outcomes from explicit operation dependencies.

cases.contract: Restart preserves only acknowledged durable volume state, recreates volatile package state, retains stable node identity and address, and increments incarnation.
cases.replacement: V2 restarts translated functions in one process and does not prove hard isolation or in-flight packet fate; v3 separates modeled durability from volatile runtime state and binds traffic to incarnations.

cases.contract: Repeated execution with the same seed, spec, backend identity, and inputs produces equal detached transition and outcome identities.
Two independently addressed nodes can run registered boot functions and complete one deterministic request/response over configured directional links.
